title: Deep learning's false-positive burden threatens the MRI harm-reduction mandate in screening
subtitle_or_tagline: Göteborg Prostate Screening 2 — specificity drops up to 0.37 below radiologists in low-prevalence cohorts
topic: A European Radiology commentary analyzing findings from the Göteborg Prostate Cancer Screening 2 Trial, where a deep-learning model exhibited a specificity drop of up to 0.37 versus radiologists when applied to a low-prevalence screening cohort after development on symptomatic hospital populations. The resulting false-positive burden drives unnecessary biopsies, directly threatening the harm-reduction mandate that justifies MRI-based screening. The authors warn that models trained on symptomatic hospital populations cannot be dropped into healthy screening populations without rigorous validation and recalibration.

workflow_steps: Step 1 - Train DL model on symptomatic hospital MRI cohorts
Step 2 - Deploy to low-prevalence screening population without recalibration
Step 3 - Measure specificity against radiologist readers in the trial
Step 4 - Observe up to 0.37 specificity drop -> false-positive biopsy burden
Step 5 - Recognize the generalization gap: validation and recalibration are mandatory before population deployment

caveats_or_warnings: Commentary on a single trial (Göteborg 2) — prostate MRI specific
The generalization-gap lesson generalizes, but the magnitude (0.37) is domain-specific

osiris_connection: This is a population-scale demonstration of why c must be recalibrated per deployment regime. The model's operating point — implicitly its (L, c) pair — was calibrated on a hospital distribution where prevalence justified a permissive displacement budget; the screening population shifts the prior, and the same budget that was 'permissive' in clinic becomes 'harmful' in screening: every unit of displacement budget the model spends now converts into biopsies at population scale. OSIRIS's disease presets embody the correct pattern — cancer c=2.5σ for heterogeneous clinical tissue, Alzheimer c=1.8σ for pre-clinical sensitivity — the clamp radius is a deployment-regime parameter, not a model constant. The Göteborg result is the cost of treating it as a constant: a 0.37 specificity collapse is what an unrecalibrated bound looks like in the wild.
